ordered_diagnoses: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with median nerve compression
salient_findings: Mass on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
key_facts: 23-year-old man
1-year history of a gradually enlarging mass
Mass located on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
Mass located along the radial edge
Phalen’s maneuver was positive
Durkan’s test was positive
Magnetic resonance imaging of the wrist was performed
Mass was well-defined and encapsulated on MRI
Mass exhibited biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign) on MRI

differentials: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
per_call: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of wrist mass with median nerve compression

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
shortlist.why_kept: Typically presents as a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the wrist

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and exhibit biphasic contrast enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the wrist with nerve compression

shortlist.label: Fibroma of tendon sheath
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and exhibit a well-defined, encapsulated appearance on MRI

raw.rationale: The mass is well-defined, encapsulated, and exhibits biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign) on MRI, which is characteristic of a ganglion cyst. Additionally, the location on the radial edge of the wrist and the positive Phalen’s and Durkan’s tests suggesting median nerve compression are consistent with a ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
rejected.why: While possible, giant cell tumors of tendon sheath are less common and typically do not exhibit the same characteristic MRI findings as ganglion cysts.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are less likely given the location and MRI characteristics, which do not suggest a nerve sheath tumor.

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically found under the fingernail and are less likely given the location on the wrist.

rejected.label: Fibroma of tendon sheath
rejected.why: Fibroma of tendon sheath is less common and does not typically exhibit the same MRI characteristics as ganglion cysts.
